findings.title: Worker text is copied verbatim into a memory record with no handling of hostile content
quotes: the first two under `## What is wrong`, the third under `## Proposed change`
each of the three texts appears verbatim under its section
findings.fix: add an AC for hostile and empty `change_request` texts. Either neutralise heading and front-matter lines, or refuse the handoff loudly. State the size bound and the concurrent-run behaviour (one record).

sources.situation: a worker is an untrusted writer. Its `change_request` holds a line like `## Proposed change`, a `---` front-matter delimiter, or a fake `Status: decided`. It may also be empty, or megabytes long.

findings.reason: FR-2 and AC-2 require verbatim copy of worker text under fixed headings. Nothing in the spec handles heading, front-matter or empty text, so a `change_request` containing `## Proposed change` would break the record's sections and the memory check that AC-1 depends on.
findings.note: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-16, AC-20, AC-21: block refuses a change_request text with a '## ' or '---' line, or an empty text, and files nothing; it already files under the effort lock (RF-17); size noted in Risks.

findings.title: A deferral can remove every test requirement from a task, and nothing checks the target is real
quotes: then red is accepted with no file requirement
A TC a later task proves only in part counts as deferred
fail for a deferred TC ID that the task its `Test:` line names doesn't cite as its own
findings.fix: have FR-12 also require that the target task exists and is later. Say which reading wins when a TC is both own and deferred. Decide whether a task may defer all of its TCs (AC-6) and what stops that being a bypass. Re-check the target when tasks are removed.

sources.situation: UJ-2's misuse is "the command names an unrelated file only to get past the check".

findings.reason: FR-12 only requires that the named task cites the TC as its own. It does not require that task to be later than the deferring one, and nothing says which reading wins when a TC is both own and deferred on the same line. AC-6 lets a task defer every TC it cites, which removes its file requirement. A nonexistent target is probably caught, since it cites nothing, so the "target is real" part of the finding is weaker than the rest.
findings.note: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-3, AC-23: a TC cited outside the deferral part is own (own wins); deferring every TC is caught at the tasks jury (Risks); the later-task check moved out with #69 (non-goals).

findings.title: Tasks under Fixes bypass approval, and a judged task can be moved there
quotes: keep it approved when a task is added under `#### Fixes`
without making a lens re-run on that alone
findings.fix: define "added under Fixes" as an ID never seen at the judged version. Treat a changed or moved judged ID as a normal change that triggers a re-run. Say who may add fix tasks and whether a limit applies.

sources.situation: FR-8 and FR-7 let any task under `#### Fixes` go through with no juror verdict and no re-approval. Nothing bounds the number or scope of such tasks, so unreviewed work accumulates under an approved gate.

findings.reason: The Decisions entry ("shown to the juror but doesn't make a lens re-run or withdraw an approval") and FR-8 [research: RF-9] make this behaviour deliberate. The Glossary defines a fix task as "added after the tasks gate judged the list", which settles that it is a new task. Unbounded accumulation is a design choice, not a contradiction or gap in the artefact.

findings.title: With NIO_PERF off, the speed requirement is enforced nowhere
quotes: assert its time limit only when `NIO_PERF=1` is set
without any wall-clock limit that load can exceed
findings.fix: name one place and one trigger where `NIO_PERF=1` runs, with an AC for it. Narrow FR-11 to the named speed assertions, or list which timing checks remain.

sources.situation: after this change the status-speed and drift-speed limits are never asserted in the default run. No AC, FR or entry says where `NIO_PERF=1` is run (CI, a scheduled run, before release). A 10x slowdown of `nio flow status` then passes every review and gate, and the "NFR-3: status in under 2 seconds" requirement quietly loses its only check.

findings.title: The evaluator's "only rating lines" rule is enforced by the card and tool choice alone
quotes: change only the tasks' `Tier:`, `Effort:` and `Mode:` lines in `tasks.md`
with an edit tool and no whole-file write tool
findings.fix: add a deterministic post-run check, for example that the diff of `tasks.md` touches only rating lines, run by `nio check tasks` or the flow, with an AC that rejects a stray edit.

sources.situation: the evaluator reads task text that workers and drafters wrote, so injected text in a task could steer it. An edit tool can still change any line, such as a task's `Test:` or `Files:` line. Edits keyed on a repeated `Tier: standard` line can also land on the wrong task silently.

findings.title: Own TC IDs: refuse when any file is missing, or only when none is named
quotes: → refused, naming the missing file; an attempt is used
IF `nio flow red` refuses a command for naming none of the required test files THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL name only the required files in the refusal.
findings.fix: say whether the command must name every required file or at least one. Make the table row, FR-4 and FR-3 use the same wording, and add an AC with two own TC IDs.

sources.situation: a task's `Test:` line cites own TC-10 and TC-12, which have different files, and the red command names only TC-10's file. The decision table row `own | no` refuses it for TC-12's missing file and spends an attempt. FR-4 refuses only a command naming none of the required files, so this command is accepted. The same input gets two outcomes. AC-5 only covers one own TC, so it settles neither reading.

findings.reason: The decision table row `own | no` refuses for any missing own file, while FR-4 speaks of a command "naming none of the required test files". With two own TC IDs and only one file named, the two readings give different outcomes. AC-4 and AC-5 cover only one own TC and settle neither.
findings.note: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-3, FR-4, red table: the command must name a file of at least one own TC ID, as today; AC-22 covers two own TCs.

findings.title: Fix-task rows say "shown and listed", but FR-7 and FR-8 add "no re-run", which the table and ACs don't carry
quotes: → shown in the fix-check pack and listed by `changed`
without making a lens re-run on that alone
then T-30 is among the changed IDs it reports
findings.fix: add a column to the decision table for "makes a lens re-run" (no for Fixes, yes for the other rows). Add an AC for a Fixes-only change that asserts no re-run. State what happens to approval when a task is removed.

sources.situation: the only change since the judged version is T-30 added under `#### Fixes`. `nio jury changed` lists T-30 as a changed ID, exactly as it lists an added task outside Fixes, which the table treats the same way. Nothing says what separates "listed, no re-run" from "listed, re-run". AC-10 tests only that the gate stays approved. Nothing tests that no lens is asked to re-run, and nothing covers a Fixes task together with a removal. In AC-8, T-4 is removed while the gate is approved. findings.title: FR-11 bans any load-exceedable time limit, but FR-15 and the Decisions entry keep some
quotes: THE SYSTEM SHALL decide the result without any wall-clock limit that load can exceed.
time-limit tests keep their wide bounds
with `NIO_PERF=1` set, they assert their 2-second limits as today
findings.fix: reword FR-11 as "without any wall-clock assertion unless `NIO_PERF=1`". Say the review never sets `NIO_PERF`. Say what a wide-bound test is allowed to assert.

sources.situation: a review runs the full suite on a loaded machine and `NIO_PERF=1` is set in the environment. Status over 20 efforts takes 2.5 seconds, the 2-second assertion fires, and the review fails. FR-11 forbids that outcome and FR-15 allows it. The same applies to the "wide bounds" tests. A wide bound is still a wall-clock limit that enough load can exceed, so FR-11 forbids it too. AC-14 does not say that `NIO_PERF` is unset, and AC-18 does not say a review never sets it.

any time limit can be exceeded under enough load, so "any wall-clock limit that load can exceed" has no pass or fail condition. AC-14 does not say how 2.5 s is produced (a sleep injected into status? a patched clock?). Nor does it say whether `NIO_PERF` is unset in that run. If `NIO_PERF=1` is inherited, the 2-second test fails by design. SC-5 ("when the machine is idle") cannot be checked either.

FR-11 says a review must never depend on a limit load can exceed, and FR-15 only moves "speed requirement" limits behind NIO_PERF. Under the Decisions bullet, a "time-limit" test with a wide bound (for example a 10-second assertion in the suite) keeps running on every review. On a loaded machine it can fail and spend a task attempt, which is the failure US-5 exists to stop. The spec never defines the split between "speed requirement" and "time-limit" tests, so a builder can't tell which side a test falls on.

findings.reason: FR-11 forbids any load-exceedable wall-clock limit, while FR-15 and the Decisions keep a 2-second limit under `NIO_PERF=1` and "wide bounds" on other time-limit tests. Nothing says a review runs with `NIO_PERF` unset, so FR-11 and FR-15 can conflict.
findings.note: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-11 now says the review strips NIO_PERF; FR-15 names only test_nfr3_status_speed; the 'wide bounds' decision is gone and time-limit tests are a non-goal.

findings.title: AC-13 judges a real model from a single run
quotes: when the evaluator rates it on a real model
findings.fix: require the run to rate at least one task (non-empty diff) and say how many runs or fixtures count. Or add a deterministic check that rejects any diff line that is not a rating line.

sources.situation: a model that is non-deterministic can pass one run and rewrite epic headings on the next. One green e2e run does not show FR-9 holds. The same run could also fail because the model rated nothing, since the AC only says changed lines must be rating lines, not that any were changed. That is a vacuous pass.

the evaluator reads task text that workers and drafters wrote, so injected text in a task could steer it. An edit tool can still change any line, such as a task's `Test:` or `Files:` line. Edits keyed on a repeated `Tier: standard` line can also land on the wrong task silently.

findings.reason: AC-13's Observable only requires that every changed line is a rating line. An empty diff, where nothing was rated, satisfies it, and it names a single real-model run (Level: e2e). Nothing else in the spec (FR-9, FR-10, SC-4) adds a non-empty requirement or a deterministic check on the diff.
findings.note: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): AC-13 (one real-model run) retired; FR-9 is now a deterministic nio check tasks --rated-from <copy> (AC-26, AC-27), run by the tasks skill (FR-17, AC-28).
